issues.legal_issue: A conditional letter of intent that contemplates a later sale agreement does not create an enforceable right to specific performance when the purchaser has not fulfilled its conditions and no formal sale agreement has been executed.
material_facts: The developer issued letters of intent reserving flats subject to stated conditions, including payment of installments, and contemplated executing sale agreements after payment of the purchase price.
The purchasers stopped paying installments, including amounts due under the original terms, and did not fulfill the conditions in the letters of intent.
No formal sale agreements were executed.
issues.conclusion: The letters of intent did not create a binding contract for sale, and the purchasers were not entitled to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(1) of the Maharashtra Ownership of Flats (Regulation of Promotion of Construction, Sale, Management and Transfer) Act, 1963, an agreement between a flat purchaser and a developer is to be registered. The conditional letters of intent were not sale agreements: they contemplated a later agreement after payment and fulfillment of conditions. The court held that, absent a registered agreement and fulfillment of the conditions, no enforceable right to specific performance arose.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and conditional_reservation_letter and required_conditions_unfulfilled and formal_sale_agreement_absent

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a suit seeking specific performance of an asserted agreement to buy a flat.
predicates.conditional_reservation_letter: The developer issued a letter reserving a flat subject to conditions and contemplating a later sale agreement.
predicates.required_conditions_unfulfilled: The purchaser did not fulfill the conditions required for the proposed purchase.
predicates.formal_sale_agreement_absent: The developer and purchaser did not execute a formal sale agreement.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeks specific performance based on a conditional reservation, but has not fulfilled its conditions and no formal sale agreement was executed, specific performance is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent purchaser is treated as a bona fide purchaser for consideration where the prior purchasers did not plead bad faith or notice, the prior transaction was unregistered, and notice of it was not established.
material_facts: The developer later sold the flats to other buyers, who asserted that they paid consideration and had no notice of the earlier transactions.
The earlier transactions were not registered, and the subsequent buyers therefore had no registered document to inspect as notice of those transactions.
The original purchasers did not plead that the subsequent buyers were not bona fide purchasers for consideration.
The original purchasers did not establish that the subsequent buyers knew of the earlier transactions.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent buyers were bona fide purchasers for consideration without notice.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on Ram Swarup Gupta (dead) through LRs. v. Bishun Narain Inter College and Ors. for the principle that a court will not decide a case beyond the pleadings. Where the purchasers allege that subsequent buyers lacked good faith or had notice, that allegation must be pleaded; ordinarily, the burden of proving notice rests on the purchasers, unless a registered document gives rise to a presumption of knowledge. The court also held that an unregistered prior agreement did not give the subsequent buyers an opportunity to inspect it or justify presuming their knowledge of it.

rule.if: dispute_over_subsequent_purchaser and prior_transaction_unregistered and bad_faith_or_notice_not_pleaded and notice_not_established and consideration_paid

predicates.dispute_over_subsequent_purchaser: A claim concerning a property sale was contested on the basis that a later purchaser had notice of an earlier transaction or lacked good faith.
predicates.prior_transaction_unregistered: The earlier transaction between the original purchaser and seller was not registered.
predicates.bad_faith_or_notice_not_pleaded: The original purchaser did not plead that the later purchaser lacked good faith or had notice of the earlier transaction.
predicates.notice_not_established: The original purchaser did not establish that the later purchaser knew of the earlier transaction.
predicates.consideration_paid: The later purchaser paid consideration for the property.

issues.definition: Where a later purchaser paid consideration, the earlier transaction was unregistered, and bad faith or notice was neither pleaded nor established, the later purchaser is treated as bona fide.

issues.legal_issue: Purchasers who cannot obtain specific performance of an unfulfilled and unformalized flat-purchase arrangement are entitled to repayment of amounts paid, with interest, and the rate may be increased in light of rising prices and inflation.
material_facts: The purchasers had paid installments to the developer but had not fulfilled the purchase conditions or obtained formal sale agreements.
The High Court denied specific performance and directed the developer to refund the amounts received with interest from the date of cancellation.
The Supreme Court considered that refund direction just and proper but increased the interest rate in view of rising prices and inflation.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers were entitled to a refund with interest, and the interest rate ordered by the High Court was increased.
issues.legal_principle: The court upheld the refund remedy as just and proper and increased the interest in light of rising prices and inflation. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this modification.

rule.if: appeal_in_specific_performance_dispute and purchaser_paid_installments and specific_performance_unavailable and rising_cost_conditions

predicates.appeal_in_specific_performance_dispute: An appeal concerned a dispute in which a purchaser sought specific performance of a flat-purchase arrangement.
predicates.purchaser_paid_installments: The purchaser paid installments to the developer toward the proposed purchase.
predicates.specific_performance_unavailable: The purchaser was not entitled to specific performance of the proposed purchase.
predicates.rising_cost_conditions: The court considered rising prices and inflation relevant to the appropriate interest on the refund.

issues.definition: In an appeal involving a purchaser who paid installments but cannot obtain specific performance, rising cost conditions may result in a refund being ordered with increased interest.
